headline: Vol came home and took gold with it — the hedge of last resort is now a source of funds, and only Treasuries worked.
summary: Yesterday's calm was a one-day lie. VIX +15.8% to 28.44 after a -8.6% session, VIX3M +11.3% to 27.03, and the term structure flipped back into backwardation at 1.0522 (+4.1%, z=1.72) — both tenors now carry one-month z-scores above 2.5, which is a regime, not a spike. The index damage was undifferentiated: SPX -2.0% to 7,175.8, NDX -2.2%, DJI -2.2%, RUT -2.2%. When every index prints the same number, you are watching index-level de-grossing, not stock-picking. Asia is already marking it forward: N225 -3.9% to 56,701 (z=-2.53, acc -1.42), KOSPI -3.1% (-14.4% on the month), ASX -2.1%. Note the sector and ETF prints in this digest are dated 11/18 and therefore understate the damage by a full session.

What is genuinely new versus yesterday is that the metal itself got sold. Yesterday copper rose and gold fell only 0.9% while COPX, GDX and FCX were destroyed — forced selling of levered equity. Today gold -3.9% to 3,594.8 (z=-2.93, 0th percentile of its 52-week range, -21.4% over three months), silver -5.7% to 42.43, platinum -2.5%, GLD -3.2%, DBC -2.3%, copper -1.7%. Gold/silver jumped to 84.72, +18.0% on the month at z=2.64 and the 100th percentile — the textbook signature of a collateral call, not a macro view. Against that, duration finally did its job: 10y -3bp to 5.07%, 30y -5bp to 5.41%, TLT +0.8% with acceleration z=+0.53, IEF +0.3%, LQD +0.4%, and MOVE -2.2% to 96.0, now -5.6% on the month. Bond volatility is flatly refusing to confirm equity volatility. That is the single most reassuring print on the board and it is why this is a de-leveraging, not yet a funding accident.

The slow leak is credit and it is accelerating in exactly the wrong cohort. CCC spreads +24bp to 13.53, +43bp on the month and +323bp over three months, sitting at the 99.4th percentile. HY +4bp to 3.47 (98.9th percentile, +74bp over three months), BBB +1bp to 1.16 with a one-month z of 1.00, IG +1bp to 0.93 at z=0.91. HYG is unchanged and HYG/IEF -0.3% — the ETF is lying about the index. The dollar is the other transmission channel: DXY 103.88 at the 100th percentile, USDCAD and USDMXN also at 100, and USDBRL +0.9% to 5.9346, now +18.2% on the month at z=5.04 with acceleration z=3.94, still the most violent series anywhere in this dataset. EWZ -28.3% on the month, ARGT -20.5%, Bovespa -20.1%. AUDUSD -0.9% (z=-1.92) and AUDJPY -0.8% (-4.3% on the month, z=-1.70) confirm from the G10 side. Crypto remains the purest read on marginal leverage: BTC 62,232 (-25.9% on the month), ETH -28.7%, SOL -31.4%, MSTR -33.6%, COIN -34.4%.

The offsets are intact and they are all disinflation. Ten-year breakevens at 2.16 (z=-1.30, literally the 0th percentile of the year), five-year at 2.22 after -17bp in a month, gasoline -20.8% and WTI -18.6% over the same window. That is a direct rebate to the consumer and a permission slip for the Fed — and the consumer tape is already pricing it: UPS +15.6%, MCD +12.9%, COST +10.3%, HD +9.0%, TGT +9.0%, WMT +7.3% over one month, with XRT/SPY at z=1.86. Breadth still will not break: RSP/SPY +6.0% monthly at z=2.89 with acceleration 1.83, IYT/SPY z=2.76 acceleration 2.06, IWM/SPY z=1.48 acceleration 1.91, and equal-weight SPW +1.0% on the month against NDX -10.1%. Labour is fine — claims 203k, continuing 1.763m, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), unemployment 4.1%. The problem is the real yield: 10y TIPS at 2.88%, 94th percentile, 27.3% above its 200-day. Nominals sticky, breakevens at zero percentile — that is passive tightening and it is why 2s10s sits at 28bp with acceleration -0.55. Two frictions worsened today: the 30-year mortgage backed up 17bp on the week to 7.28%, which takes some air out of the homebuilder bid, and the risk regime slipped to -19 from -17. Inflation composite 55 against a growth pulse of -11 remains the whole argument.

good.text: Treasuries finally hedged. 10y -3bp to 5.07%, 30y -5bp to 5.41%, TLT +0.8% with acceleration z=+0.53, IEF +0.3% — and MOVE fell 2.2% to 96.0 (-5.6% on the month) while VIX rose 15.8%. Bond vol is not confirming equity vol; this is a de-grossing, not a funding break.

The disinflation impulse is now extreme: 10y breakevens 2.16 at the 0th percentile (z=-1.30, acc -0.93), 5y 2.22 after -17bp in a month, gasoline -20.8% and WTI -18.6% over the same window. Real income tailwind plus a rate-cut permission slip.

Breadth still refuses to confirm the index damage. Equal-weight/cap-weight +6.0% on the month at z=2.89 with acceleration 1.83, transports/S&P z=2.76 acceleration 2.06, small caps/S&P z=1.48 acceleration 1.91, and SPW +1.0% monthly against NDX -10.1%.
Consumer and logistics are the identifiable leadership: UPS +15.6%, MCD +12.9%, COST +10.3%, HD +9.0%, TGT +9.0%, WMT +7.3% on the month, XRT +4.0% with XRT/SPY at z=1.86 and relative strength +9.2%.

Labour is not cracking. Initial claims 203k (-11.0% y/y), continuing claims 1.763m (-9.4% y/y), JOLTS openings 7,523 (+4.6%), unemployment 4.1% and 30bp lower on the year. No recession is being signalled by the household side yet.
India is the one market compounding through the stress: Sensex +11.1% on the month at z=2.61 with acceleration 2.04, INDA +8.6% and relative strength +14.0%, helped by USDINR -1.5% on cheap crude.

bad.text: The vol regime re-established itself in one session: VIX +15.8% to 28.44, VIX3M +11.3% to 27.03, term structure inverted at 1.0522 (+4.1%, z=1.72). One-month z-scores of 2.55 and 2.61 with acceleration 1.21 and 1.50 — this is a faster sell-off, not a cleansing spike.

Gold itself is now being liquidated, not just the miners. Gold -3.9% to 3,594.8 at the 0th percentile (z=-2.93), silver -5.7%, platinum -2.5%, GLD -3.2%, and gold/silver at 84.72, 100th percentile, z=2.64. Hedges sold for cash is a late-stage margin signature.

Credit keeps widening and the junk end is accelerating: CCC +24bp to 13.53 (99.4th percentile, +323bp in three months), HY +4bp to 3.47 (98.9th percentile), BBB z=1.00, IG z=0.91. HYG unchanged and HYG/IEF -0.3% — the ETF is understating the index.

LatAm funding stress has not peaked. USDBRL +0.9% to 5.9346, +18.2% on the month at z=5.04 with acceleration z=3.94; USDMXN +1.3% to 19.104 at the 100th percentile; EWZ -28.3% monthly; ARGT -20.5%; Bovespa -20.1% with acceleration -4.05.

Asia tech took another leg and is leading the world lower: Nikkei -3.9% (z=-2.53), KOSPI -3.1% and -14.4% on the month, TAIEX -14.2% monthly at z=-2.65, SMH -16.2% with SMH/SPY at z=-2.01, NVDA -30.5% on the month and pinned at the 0th percentile.

The momentum unwind is intact and the housing offset is fading: high beta/low vol -13.5% monthly at z=-2.13, MTUM z=-2.18, growth/value z=-2.23 at the 4th percentile — while the 30-year mortgage backed up 17bp on the week to 7.28%.

trades.name: Duration over credit
trades.line: Long TLT vs short HYG: own the bond, not the borrower
trades.expr: Long TLT, short HYG, dollar-neutral. Alternative expression: long Dec 10y note futures against a short in CDX HY.
trades.thesis: Breakevens at the 0th percentile with crude -18.6% on the month means the inflation leg of the bear case is gone; nominal 10s at 5.07% and real 10s at 2.88% (94th percentile) have room to fall. Meanwhile the credit cycle is still widening: CCC at the 99.4th percentile and BBB at a one-month z of 1.00. You want the risk-free cash flow and not the levered one.
trades.trigger: Today 10y -3bp, 30y -5bp, TLT +0.8% with acceleration z=+0.53 and MOVE -2.2% to 96.0 — while CCC widened 24bp in a single print and HY added 4bp to 3.47. The two are diverging for the first time in weeks.
trades.stop: HY spread tightening back below 3.20 with CCC under 13.00 while 10y yields push above 5.25% — that is a growth-reacceleration tape and both legs lose.
trades.target: 10y toward 4.70%, HY toward 4.00%; roughly +7% on the combined pair.

trades.name: De-gross beta into inverted vol
trades.line: Long SPLV vs short SPHB while the VIX curve is backward
trades.expr: Long SPLV, short SPHB in equal dollars. Overlay: sell SPY 1-month 5-delta puts only if VIX/VIX3M falls back under 0.97.
trades.thesis: An inverted VIX term structure with both tenors at one-month z above 2.5 is not a buyable dip; it is a liquidity event in progress. High beta has already lost 13.5% to low vol in a month at z=-2.13 and the ratio is still rolling over, which means the de-grossing has not been completed by the slow money.
trades.trigger: VIX +15.8% to 28.44, VIX3M +11.3% to 27.03, VIX/VIX3M 1.0522 (+4.1%, z=1.72, acceleration 1.21/1.50). All four major US indices fell the same 2.0-2.2% — indiscriminate index selling.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.95 with VIX under 22 and SPHB/SPLV reclaiming its 200-day; close the pair.
trades.target: Another 6-8% of relative outperformance; SPHB/SPLV toward 1.52.

trades.name: Gasoline rebate, long the spender short the driller
trades.line: Long XRT vs short XOP: -21% gasoline is a consumer rebate
trades.expr: Long XRT, short XOP, equal dollars. Size the short to roughly 0.8x on beta given XOP's higher volatility.
trades.thesis: A 20.8% monthly collapse in RBOB and an 18.6% drop in WTI is a multi-billion dollar transfer from E&P cash flow to household discretionary income. The retail tape is already confirming it and the producer tape is already denying it is over. Energy equity still has further to catch down: XLE is only -9.6% on the month against crude -18.6%.
trades.trigger: Brent -2.4% today to 89.72, WTI rolling over at z=-1.86; XOP -3.4% and -14.0% on the month at z=-1.72 while XRT +2.3% with XRT/SPY at z=1.86 and relative strength +9.2%.
trades.stop: WTI reclaiming $90 (a supply shock, not demand), or XRT/SPY breaking back below its 200-day.

trades.name: Brazil contagion's next domino
trades.line: Long USDMXN vs short EWW: Mexico hasn't priced the stress
trades.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month forward, short EWW against half the notional. Cleanest single expression: 3-month USD/MXN 19.50 calls.
trades.thesis: Brazil is done being a surprise — USDBRL is +18.2% in a month at z=5.04 and EWZ is -28.3%. Mexico is the same funding complex at a fraction of the move: EWW is only -2.3% on the month while USDMXN is already at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range. Either Brazil mean-reverts or Mexico converges; the risk-reward is on convergence.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +1.3% today to 19.104, +3.7% on the month at z=1.35; USDBRL still accelerating at z=3.94; CEW -0.7% and -2.0% on the month at z=-1.19; DXY at the 100th percentile.
trades.stop: USDBRL closing back below 5.60 and USDMXN below 18.60 — the LatAm funding squeeze has resolved and this trade is a late entry.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH: the capex payer beats the capex taker
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal dollars. Express with options by buying IGV 3-month 25-delta calls financed by SMH 25-delta calls.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is unwinding through the hardware end first because that is where the leverage, the Asian supply chain and the dollar funding sit. Software/semis has already turned: the ratio is +9.2% on the month at z=1.36 with the trend turning up, and it is still 32.9% below where it was a year ago — the unwind has a long way left.
trades.trigger: IGV +1.3% today against SMH -0.1%; SMH -16.2% on the month with SMH/SPY at z=-2.01; NVDA -30.5% monthly at the 0th percentile; TAIEX -14.2% and KOSPI -14.4% on the month, with the Korean and Taiwanese cash markets down another 3.1% and the Nikkei 3.9% overnight.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.195, or a semis capitulation bounce that takes SMH/SPY above its 200-day.
trades.target: IGV/SMH toward 0.235, roughly +10% on the pair.

trades.name: India over Korea
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWY: oil importer beats chip exporter
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EWY, equal dollars.
trades.thesis: Cheap crude is a terms-of-trade windfall for India and a non-event for Korea, which is instead levered to the semiconductor cycle that is breaking. One is the only accelerating equity market on the board; the other is a 29% three-month drawdown with its currency starting to go the wrong way.
trades.trigger: Sensex +11.1% on the month at z=2.61 with acceleration 2.04 and INDA relative strength +14.0%, while KOSPI -3.1% today and -14.4% on the month, EWY -12.7% monthly, and USDKRW +1.0% with acceleration z=1.58. USDINR -1.5% on the month on the oil collapse.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 95 (the import windfall reverses), or EWY outperforming INDA by more than 7%, which would mean the semi cycle has bottomed.
trades.target: +12% on the pair over two months.

trades.name: Buy the margin-called hedge
trades.line: Long GLD: gold got margin-called, not repriced
trades.expr: Long GLD, half size, scaling in. Prefer 3-month 25-delta GLD call spreads to cap the knife-catch risk.
trades.thesis: Gold at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, -13.2% in a month and -21.4% in three, with silver -5.7% in a day and gold/silver at the 100th percentile, is the signature of a liquidation for cash, not a change in the macro case. The macro case is actually improving at the margin: nominal 10s fell 8bp over the month and breakevens are at the 0th percentile only because oil collapsed, so the next move in real yields from 2.88% (94th percentile, 27.3% above its 200-day) is lower once growth data soften.
trades.trigger: Gold -3.9% today at a one-month z of -2.93 with acceleration -1.01 — the capitulation leg, arriving the same day VIX went to 28.44 and the VIX curve inverted. Forced sellers finish fast.
trades.stop: GLD below 320 on a close, or the 10-year real yield breaking above 3.05% — then the repricing is real and not a margin call.
